initiative.title: Change chart settings where the data is
initiative.summary: Make frequent chart changes local and clear while keeping ordinary click-to-filter primary.
initiative.next_action: Review the proposed shape, then authorize the bounded local Color proof if desired.

claims.statement: Make frequent chart changes close to the feature being edited.
Ground the proposal in verified mechanics from other visualization tools.
Compare a wide range of interaction approaches and chart settings.
Give ordinary click-to-filter priority over other gesture claims.
Allow Alt-click and tracing access to be redesigned.
Right-click a scatter point and choose Color by to pick a field.
Treat frequency rankings as hypotheses because no telemetry was supplied.

conflicts.description: Repository docs reserve Alt-click for tracing. The latest user direction explicitly allows that binding to change.
conflicts.resolution: Treat the binding as current behavior, not a proposed-design invariant. Preserve click-to-filter as the stronger constraint.

options.premise: One existing editor with exact contextual navigation
Named object actions choose a local task
Visible encoding roles serve as the control surface
Chart geometry directly represents editable values
A deliberate object toolbar groups repeated edits
An explicit mode changes gesture ownership

brainstorm.selected_option: Compare option-3 alone with option-3 plus option-2; retain existing option-4 and option-1 fallback.

shape.appetite: One scatter Color proof, then reassess. Research and docs only in this run.
shape.problem: Repeated chart changes require navigation away from the question. Hidden configuration can also conflict with filtering.
shape.recommended_shape: Visible encoding control plus shallow object menu opening the same compact editor; conditional Alt experiment.

success_moves.move: Compare a visible-only Color selector before adding menu or modifier complexity.
success_moves.effect: A simpler design can win the proof.

success_moves.move: Resolve chart scope without requiring exact record identity.
success_moves.effect: Dense overlapping points do not block chart configuration.

success_moves.move: Commit only explicit field acceptance and hold notifications before scale creation.
success_moves.effect: Avoid preview rollback and duplicate host checkpoints.

success_moves.move: Reuse field metadata, scale resolution, and updateChart through a small popup presentation seam.
success_moves.effect: No generic command or transaction platform is required.

success_moves.move: Keep filtering immediate; verify input, focus, and scope before broader adoption.
Include docs and examples in every proposed visible slice.
success_moves.effect: Gesture changes remain discoverable and reviewable.

first_proof.question: Does local Color configuration improve actual exploration enough to justify menu and modifier complexity?
first_proof.artifact: Future local dense-chart-controls demo and task observation record; not produced in this research run.
first_proof.try: Filtered scatter points/bubbles, a shared-scale peer, no legend, categorical/numeric/computed fields, cancellation, keyboard, and optional Alt variant.
first_proof.observe: Discovery, scope, actions, corrections, selected field, unchanged filters/peers, focus, host checkpoint count.
first_proof.decision_rule: Reject filter/scope regressions. Keep the smallest route that improves locality or discovery; adopt Alt only if repeated changes improve and trace stays findable.
first_proof.first_dependency_role: Real local React UI and store with synthetic rows; no remote provider.
first_proof.fallback: Keep existing settings and trace convention; visible Color alone may satisfy the outcome.

rabbit_holes: Generic chart conversion or X/Y swap

open_decisions.resolution: Observe the bounded proof before deciding.

open_decisions.question: Does persistent Color visibility earn its chart space?
open_decisions.resolution: Compare persistent and focus-revealed controls with a touch-visible route.
